summary: Yes, the normalized and streaming pelvis fields describe the same physical stride. All 7,224 normalized strides in the 44 T03 treadmill recordings bind exactly (explicit StrideDetails side and frames, consecutive same-side heel strikes, duration = end - start; no concatenation order used). For every one, all three normalized pelvis components equal the same-side streaming pelvis resampled to the same 150 points (largest difference 2.8e-14 deg, no missing-value or zero-fill differences). The opposite-side streaming pelvis matches tilt but fails obliquity and rotation in all 7,224 (left and right tilt are identical, so tilt cannot tell them apart); a sign-flipped pelvis fails everywhere. A same-side hip control matches 7,224/7,224 with the 1-based frame base and 0 with a one-frame shift. AB04/i0 normalized carries the same reversed pelvis as streaming, so the two are not independent evidence there. No planar formula adopted; canonical 3D unapproved; not scientific approval.

decision_reason: Not needed. The two pelvis hypotheses do not both remain plausible: the opposite-side hypothesis fails obliquity and rotation in 7,224 of 7,224 strides. The only place they agree (tilt) is the sagittal component, so the planar release is the same either way.
findings_for_followup: 768 of the 7,562 released observations have no Normalized stride, so they cannot be backed by the normalized series; 430 normalized strides are not in the T03 release (reason not examined).
AB04/i0: Normalized and Streaming both carry the reversed pelvis; D-UM21-P01-1 = C correction applies to both alike.
No missing values in any compared pelvis stride; the gap path was not exercised by data.
